items.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023
items.q: Bobby Shew's got a set thing that he teaches and I have a little thing that I use too... Bobby Shew was here, I’m here, Charlie Davis was here... You know I was going to ask you about that passing the part because Bobby Shew had a similar story

ctx.x: Yeah. I don’t have a question there but you’re a physically strong guy but you’re small. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

Yeah well I’m 5’5-1/2 — I was, I think I shrunk a little bit. 5’5-1/2. We have a book here called The Kenton Chronicles and it’s all guys that played with Stan, wrote pieces, and Jiggs Wiggam, you know Jiggs, trombone player — well Jiggs was my roommate on the band. And he wrote that in the book, he said, “Tommy came on and played, what was it, ‘Yesterdays’ where the trumpet goes [scats] up to high G.” And said, “He’s kind of a small guy,” he said, “but he got that out. Stan got a big smile on his face and he got…

That’s good luck right there. The Kenton band came to my college where I was at SUNY Fredonia around 1970 so of course after they left we decided to play Kenton arrangements. And in talking with you I now can recall thinking about what those guys behind me were doing. I was in the saxophone section and like we would play “Here’s That Rainy Day” and that brass build-up, the whole chart builds up to this [scats] and I remember thinking wow, are they going to get it this time.
